guides.name: Philippines
guides.title: Meetings in Manila. Then the islands.
guides.sub: We host business visitors and holiday groups from China and around the world, from the arrivals hall to the departure gate — in Mandarin, English or Filipino. This is what we tell every client before they book a flight.
guides.hostNote: Based in the Philippines and runs our desk there — distribution, operations and the people you will meet.
guides.note: Entry rules, flights and prices change. We confirm everything for your passport and dates when you book.

sections.title: Visas and arrival, by passport.

items.d: Since 16 January 2026, 14 days without a visa for tourism or business — but only when you land at Manila (NAIA) or Cebu (Mactan). The stay cannot be extended or changed to another visa. Bring a passport valid six months beyond your stay, your confirmed hotel booking and a return or onward ticket. Staying longer, or flying into Clark, Davao or another airport? Apply for a temporary visitor visa before you travel; we prepare the invitation letter and itinerary.

14 days visa-free for tourism, or 30 days if you hold a valid US, Japanese, Australian, Canadian, Schengen, Singapore or UK visa or residence permit. Coming for business meetings? Tell us — the right visa depends on what you will be doing.
A visa is needed before you travel, from a Philippine embassy or consulate. We send the invitation letter, hotel confirmation and itinerary the application asks for.
Many nationalities get 30 days visa-free on arrival; some need a visa first. Send us your passport country and we confirm what applies before you book.
Register free at etravel.gov.ph within 72 hours before you land. You get a QR code that airline check-in and immigration will ask for. Any site that charges for it is not the government's.

sections.note: Immigration officers do ask about your trip. Keep your hotel booking, return ticket and our itinerary letter on your phone or on paper. Entry rules change often — we confirm yours when you book.

items.d: Direct flights from Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Shenzhen and Xiamen — about 2½ hours from South China, 4 to 4½ from Beijing.
Direct from Shanghai, Guangzhou, Shenzhen and Quanzhou. Cebu is the better gateway for Bohol and the central islands.
Connections through Hong Kong, Singapore and Bangkok, and direct flights to Manila from Dubai and Abu Dhabi.
Clark International, two hours north of Manila, is quicker to get through — but the visa-free entry for Chinese passports does not apply there.

sections.title: Manila is six cities in one.

items.d: The established business district: banks, law firms, embassies and the long-standing hotels.
Bonifacio Global City: newer towers, regional headquarters and the most walkable streets in Manila. Where most of our clients stay.
Corporate and retail headquarters, and SM Megamall, one of the country's largest malls.
Founded in 1594 and often called the world's oldest Chinatown. Filipino-Chinese trading families, wholesalers and chambers — and the markets where you see what goods really sell for.
The convention centres — SMX and the World Trade Center — and the large resort hotels near the airport.
Clark and Subic freeports to the north for logistics and light manufacturing; Cebu for furniture, export zones and the Visayas; Davao for agriculture and Mindanao.

sections.title: How we move you around Manila.
items: Plan two meetings a day, three at most. A 10 km drive across Metro Manila can take over an hour at peak time.
A car and driver stay with you all day. The driver waits outside every meeting; nobody stands in a taxi queue.
Stay near your meetings — BGC or Makati for most weeks, closer to Binondo if your week is with the Filipino-Chinese trade.
Domestic flights and boat transfers get buffer time. On the islands the weather decides, not the timetable.
From June to November typhoons can close airports for a day. We build a spare day into trips in those months.
Grab works well if you want to move on your own; we set it up on your phone when you land.

sections.title: The details that make the trip easy.

items.d: Mandarin-speaking guides and interpreters every day of the trip; Cantonese and Hokkien on request — Hokkien is the home language of many Filipino-Chinese families.
The Philippines runs on UTC+8, like Beijing. Your office in China is awake when you are working.
WeChat works normally. Filipino business runs on Viber and Messenger, so we set up the groups with your local contacts.
Cards work in hotels and malls. Alipay and WeChat Pay are taken at some malls, hotels and duty-free shops — not everywhere. We arrange pesos and a local SIM or eSIM when you land.
Chinese restaurants we know in Binondo, Makati and BGC for the business dinners; Filipino food when you want it.
Introductions to Filipino-Chinese trading families and chambers — often the fastest way into distribution.

sections.title: Add three days. It is the part they talk about.

items.e: About an hour's flight from Manila
items.d: Limestone lagoons, island hopping and some of Asia's best beaches. Our first choice for incentive groups.

items.e: About an hour's flight, then a short boat
items.d: White Beach, sunsets and easy resorts. Good for families and first visits.

items.e: An hour from Manila, or two by ferry from Cebu
items.d: The Chocolate Hills, tarsiers, river cruises and Panglao's beaches.
Island hopping from Mactan, waterfalls and diving on the south coast; easy to pair with Bohol.
Surf, palm forests and a slower pace.

items.e: Day trips by road or ferry
items.d: Tagaytay and Taal Volcano, the walled city of Intramuros, and Corregidor island.

days: Arrive at NAIA, meet and assist, check in at BGC; briefing dinner.

Binondo, Divisoria and the Filipino-Chinese trade.
Fly to El Nido; afternoon on the beach.
Ferry to Bohol: Chocolate Hills and Loboc river.

guides.name: China
guides.title: The Canton Fair, and the five cities behind it.
guides.sub: Twice a year we take buyers from Pakistan, India, the Philippines, the Gulf and beyond to Guangzhou — and on to the factories and markets of Foshan, Dongguan, Shenzhen and Yiwu. Visa, flights, hotels, meals, interpreters and booked factory meetings, run by a team in China and in your market.
guides.hostNote: Leads our China desk — the fair, the factories and the people you will meet.
guides.note: Prices are per person, twin share, and indicative until confirmed for your departure. Spring 2027 dates are expected and visa rules change — we confirm both when you book.

sections.title: Pick your phase by what you buy.

items.d: Consumer electronics, household appliances, lighting, hardware and tools, machinery, vehicles and parts, new energy.
Housewares, kitchenware, ceramics, gifts, home décor, festive goods, furniture and building materials.
Garments, textiles, shoes, bags, toys, baby products, office supplies, food, health and medical products.

sections.note: There are three days between phases. Other tours fill them with sightseeing; we use them for factories.

items.d: The Canton Fair halls at Pazhou, plus the wholesale districts: Shahe for clothing, Yide Road for toys and stationery, Xiaobei for halal food and traders from Africa and the Gulf.
45 to 60 minutes from Guangzhou: Lecong's furniture markets, ceramics and building-material makers, and Shunde's home-appliance factories.
Electronics, shoes, toys and packaging — the factory floor behind many Canton Fair booths. Where we check production and negotiate.
Huaqiangbei's electronics markets, component and accessory suppliers, and the technology companies of the Greater Bay Area.
International Trade City: more than 75,000 booths of everyday goods — the place to fill a mixed container. A short flight from Guangzhou.

sections.title: Built for buyers from Pakistan, India, the Philippines and the Gulf.

items.d: Halal restaurants we know in Xiaobei and near Pazhou, Indian vegetarian kitchens, and Filipino food when you miss it.
Interpreters who work from Mandarin into Urdu, Hindi, Filipino or Arabic — not only English.
A TGO team member from your market travels with the group; our China team meets you at arrivals.
We flag which suppliers already hold BIS, PSQCA, BPS or UAE approvals, so what you order can clear customs at home.
We work out duty, tax and freight to your market while you negotiate — the price that matters is the one on your shelf.
Samples consolidated, factories checked, quality control before shipping, and our market teams to help you sell it.

sections.title: Your China visa, by passport.

items.d: A business (M) visa with the fair's invitation letter. We prepare the application pack and book your appointment at the visa centre.
A business visa with the fair's invitation letter, or a group visa when you travel with our group. Apply at least four weeks before you fly.
A business visa. For the 140th fair the Chinese Embassy in Dhaka made the fair's invitation letter the only mandatory document.
A visa is required. Travelling with our group, a group visa through an accredited agency is the quickest route, with no personal appearance.
UAE and Qatar passports enter China visa-free for up to 30 days, as do many European ones. Living in the Gulf on another passport? Your passport's rules apply — we check.
Online pre-registration is free and issues the invitation letter your visa needs. Bring the passport you registered with, and business cards, to collect your badge.

sections.note: Visa rules change; we confirm yours before you book.

sections.title: What we tell every first-timer.
items: Book six to eight weeks ahead: visas take time, and Guangzhou hotel rates can triple in fair weeks.
Walk the halls for your category on day one; keep the serious meetings for days two and three.
Bring business cards, and photograph every booth card and price list — we log them with you each evening.
Alipay and WeChat Pay now accept foreign cards; we set them up with you before the fair.
Google and WhatsApp do not work on Chinese networks; roaming or an eSIM from home does. We test yours when you land.
Use the days between phases for factories. The best prices are agreed at the factory, not at the booth.
Metro Line 8 stops at the fair (Xingang East and Pazhou), but we drive you — you are never in the queue.

items.q: Do I need a registered company?
items.a: No, but a business card and a clear list of what you want to buy make the visa and the meetings easier. Most of our travellers are importers, wholesalers, retailers and online sellers.
Six to eight weeks before your phase. Your visa needs the fair's invitation letter, and hotel rates rise as the fair gets closer.

items.q: Can I come on my own?
items.a: Yes. Join a group departure, or travel privately with the same hotel, interpreter and factory visits.

items.q: What happens after I get home?
items.a: That is the part we are built for: samples, factory checks, quality control, shipping, customs and certification in your market, and selling through our distribution.

items.q: Do you work with banks and chambers?
items.a: Yes. We run private delegations for banks, chambers and trade associations that send their members, with a report for the organiser.
